context.why: Merge-gate change to FS-030 from the maintainer, in two parts. (1) 'All coordinate input MUST be declared in WGS84' — no reference-system input; other systems are issue #512. (2) 'Decimal degrees only for now' — degrees and minutes, degrees/minutes/seconds and hemisphere letters go too; issue #513. A previous worker already did part 1 in the code (commit e9a2f984: reference-system input, conversion and their tests removed) and started the spec/docs updates (next commit, marked unfinished). Read `git show e9a2f984 --stat` and the last commit, then finish both parts with the smallest orthodox change: latitude and longitude are plain signed decimal-degree numbers in WGS 84, latitude -90..90, longitude -180..180, refused outside with a message, using ordinary Django number fields and validators (e.g. FloatField with MinValueValidator/MaxValueValidator) rather than custom parsing. Keep: the elevation and uncertainty rules, both coordinates go together, elevation/uncertainty need coordinates, the approved layout (latitude then longitude, elevation and uncertainty with their units), escaping. Remove: parse_coordinate's notation handling (or parse_coordinate itself if number fields do the job), the lat-lon-parser dependency from pyproject.toml and uv.lock (`uv lock`), the 'Reads as' hint and the widget script if nothing else needs it, and the 64-character cap if number inputs make it moot. Tabular import reads latitude and longitude as numbers with the same range rules, reporting a bad row and not saving it. Delete tests that only served notations, hemispheres or reference systems; keep and adapt range, pairing, elevation/uncertainty, organization and import-row tests. Update to match: spec.md (FR-006 and FR-007 become decimal degrees in WGS 84; User Story 1 text and its acceptance scenarios; Clarifications; Edge Cases; SC-001; Key Entities; Boundary points at #512 and #513), decisions.md (D6 and D11 updated to say what changed, plus one entry D29 'Coordinates are entered as decimal degrees in WGS 84' with an **ADR:** verdict line), sketch.md 'What was ruled by eye' (record the maintainer's change), plan.md D3, research.md survey rows, docs/portal-development/locations.md and every other page mentioning notations or reference systems for input (grep docs/ for 'minutes', 'EPSG', 'notation', 'lat-lon-parser', 'reference system'), CONTEXT.md, CHANGELOG.md, ADR 0032 if it mentions either.
prior_decisions: D1: a location is a value on each record, never a shared row. No Location model, no get_or_create.
D8: no data migration — existing Point data is not carried across.
D12: field names are location, location_elevation, location_uncertainty.

FR-009: a sample type shows the location input only when its registration's fields list location. The demo's RockSample registration is to list location (as the approved prototype did); WaterSample does not.

D3 (decisions): a measurement falls back to its sample's location only for a viewer who may open the sample (Sample.objects.visible_to(user)); for anyone else a measurement with no location of its own has none.
D16: location constraints are listed in each concrete model's own Meta (location_constraints()), not on LocatedRecord.Meta.
Remedies are the smallest edit that fixes the named failure; add no mechanism beyond what the task says.
Out of this cycle (do not do): TST-002 declare_addressing, TST-003, TST-004, COR-005 — they are carried to the maintainer.
